critique.evidence: Desktop is visually strong: disciplined dark palette, crisp cyan/red semantics, clear headline-to-controls-to-results hierarchy, consistent borders, and polished meters and controls. Tablet and mobile retain the design language, but the single-column card becomes excessively tall and dense; small mono labels and explanatory copy are difficult to scan, while results carry limited whitespace. The global header is less resolved: tablet/mobile navigation is visibly clipped into a horizontal rail, the SWIPE cue competes with truncated items, mobile loses the product wordmark, and underlying page text shows through behind the header. Contrast verification is also incomplete for 1 tablet and 12 mobile header nodes, so legibility is not fully proven.
critique.fix: Refine the responsive header with an opaque backdrop, stable brand treatment, and a clearer compact navigation pattern. Increase small-text size/contrast, add more sectional breathing room on mobile, and reduce tablet/mobile vertical density through tighter grouping or progressive disclosure. Verify header contrast on actual rendered backgrounds.
